name: X-Ray / Thermal Scanner
summary: Every card on the surface says OK, but inside a scanner band the product turns to X-ray and one bone of the checkout flow is fractured.
look: Clean light-mode dashboard cards on paper, crossed by a bright-edged scanner band. Inside it everything becomes near-black X-ray with bone-white glowing wireframes; a thermal pass (navy → teal → amber → coral → white) shows heat blooming around the break and cooling at the end.

components.name: Surface cards
components.role: ordinary healthy-looking UI with green '✓ OK' chips; the lie on the surface

components.name: Scanner band
components.role: bright-edged vertical band with soft bleed; everything inside is X-ray

components.name: Skeleton layer
components.role: the hidden flow (Visit → Cart → Checkout → Paid) as glowing bones and joints

components.name: Fracture
components.role: coral zigzag break between two bones; the anomaly, precisely located

components.name: Thermal LUT
components.role: navy → teal → amber → coral → white legend; heat means risk

components.name: Hot-spot readout
components.role: 'RISK 0.87 · DEPLOY #2231' callout over the heat bloom

motion.name: Band mask
motion.how: clip-path inset() window at constant speed, one frame-width per bar (2 s at 120 BPM)

motion.name: Palette switch
motion.how: X-ray → thermal via filter / feComponentTransfer cross-fade over 400 ms on a downbeat

motion.name: Heat bloom
motion.how: hot spot scales 0.9 → 1.1, sine.inOut on a 1.2 s loop; cools right→left for the CTA

story: Hook: six healthy cards pop in with green OK chips under 'And the drop still shipped on Friday.' Reveal: on the drop a scanner band slams in; inside it the cards become wireframes and the Acme mark and 'Acme Pulse' glow. Proof: in X-ray the checkout flow's bones are drawn node by node, the Cart→Checkout bone is fractured, heat blooms ('RISK 0.87 · DEPLOY #2231') and a card reads 'Checkout conversion −18% · since 09:42 · after deploy #2231' with Roll back. CTA: the thermal image cools to teal and navy behind 'Caught before customers noticed.' and Start free.
adapt: Put your own dashboard on the surface and draw your real pipeline or architecture as the skeleton; the fracture sits wherever your product finds problems.

fit.risk: Medical imagery can feel clinical or alarming; keep fractures small and always resolve them with a human decision.
